title: Event
description: One line of events/YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl (and of quests/<id>/journal.jsonl). The event log is append-only and never rewritten: readers upgrade old lines by `v` on read. `type` is `group.action`; `data` has a shape per type. Unknown types are kept by readers and ignored by renderers (forward compatible), so `type` is a pattern, not an enum; the v1 catalog is in $defs.known_types. The world sees actor.id (character) and the character's provider (tribe), never which CLI ran.
$comment: Generated by `pnpm schemas` from the zod source in packages/domain/src/schema (ADR 0003): change the zod source, never this file. Events use `v`, not `version` (implementation-plan §2.1). Secrets are redacted before append (hook, runner, store, herald). Reserved prefixes with no v1 types yet: campaign.*, battle.*, incident.*, patrol.* (stage 5), party.* and skill.* (product plan 0.5: parties and skills). One write() per line under 64 KB; readers drop a last line without a trailing newline.

id.description: ULID from IdSource; sortable by time.

quest.description: The quest after this event (questViewOf). Its id is the envelope `quest`.

max_attempts.description: budget.max_attempts: "3 attempts used" on the infirmary card.

question.description: blocked.question while it waits for the answer: the throne asks the owner to answer it.

characters.description: Characters the same step moved (characterViewOf after it): the assignee that claims or submits, the verifier that takes the review. Most character moves have no character.* type of their own.

reputation.description: reputationOf(reputation.window): the avatar ring (--rep); pct null before any verdict.

title.description: titleOf(character): the tag shown over the head, if any.

sequels.description: The line that tells a session's end: the sessions that followed the first in the same run (a reply tried once more for a tribe without structured output, a reminder of an unchanged letter, P1-33), in order. The envelope `session` is the first one's, and attempt_log has one entry for them all, so the log counts every session a run opened (P1-49).

session_id.description: The sequel's CLI session, when the runner knew it.

why.description: Why it opened: the reply tried once more, the letter unchanged (not translated).

load_trace.description: What the prompt of the session this line opens carried (PS-01b): on a session's opening line only, quest.started (an assignee's start or redispatch, a verifier's assignment), quest.unblocked (the owner's answer) and quest.resumed (mana back). Absent from every other line and from lines written before PS-01b.

scriptures.description: The scripture files the prompt carried, each whole (PS-12 brings an id per line); empty when it carried none.

file.description: The scripture's file, relative to the kingdom with `/`: the character's, then the temple's.

lines.description: Its lines as the prompt carried them, trimmed.

skills.description: The skills the prompt carried, by id; empty until stage 5 (§3.13).

blocks.description: The prompt's blocks that said something, the system part's first, each part's in order.

id.description: runner-core's PROMPT_BLOCK_IDS: decree, role, class, context_files, quest, gazetteer, scripture, skills, continuation, memos (PS-02), partial, review, resumed, answer.

chars.description: Its size in characters, trimmed: the code has no token counter (§3.16.1).

reason.description: The whole reason in one English line, for the bell and the chronicle, e.g. breaker:time: <detail>, max_attempts, script:broken: <detail>. Built from trip and detail since P1-32.

trip.description: What sent the quest there: a breaker (time, tokens, turns, commit, secrets, forbidden_paths), a review whose judges left without a verdict (no_verdict, P1-33) or kept handing in partial ones (partial_verdicts, P1-42), max_attempts, or a script-tier run (script_broken, script_usage, script_fail). Absent on lines written before P1-32.

detail.description: Absent when the trip says it all (max_attempts).

message.description: What stopped the run, as the breaker, the territory's hook, the treasury or the script said it (not translated).

patch.description: trip commit: why the Steward refused the assignee's patch for laws.patch_paths (P1-28); the next run's prompt reads it back (P1-31).

wip.description: Why the WIP commit after the breaker was refused: the work stays in the quest's plot.

paths.description: trip forbidden_paths: the paths of laws.forbidden_paths the session left changed, added or deleted in the quest's plot, relative to it with `/` (P1-49). Nothing was committed: the work stays in the plot.

apprentice_left.description: An apprentice of the session ran past its minutes or was cut at its turns: its work left belongs in a child quest (§3.12).

script.description: A script-tier quest: the catalog script that ran.

follow_up.description: trip script_fail: the follow-up quest the catalog entry opened for the failed run (P1-17).

verifiers_stopped.description: This many verifiers of the run (the envelope `attempt`) left without a verdict, stopped by a breaker (P1-23) or with no verdict in their output (P1-33), so no further one opens.

partial_verdicts.description: trip partial_verdicts: this many judges of the run (the envelope `attempt`) handed in a partial verdict since the owner last retried the review, so no further one opens (P1-42).

reason.description: no_class: no character of the class outside the suspended ones and the disabled tribes; level_too_low: even the highest level among them cannot take the rank, not even when nobody else could (canTake); party_bars: every one of them is barred by the quest's party, having judged one of its quests or worked the other side of its blind trial (partyBarsOf, P1-37); null: the reason is gone.

best_character.description: level_too_low: the highest-level character of the class.

tool.description: Normalised tool kind (implementation-plan §3.10): Read/Glob/Grep and read_file map to read, Edit/Write and write_file/replace to write, Bash and run_shell_command to bash, WebFetch/WebSearch to web.

agent_type.description: The sub-agent that made the call (`apprentice`), from the hook payload; absent when the character itself did (implementation-plan §3.12).

tool.description: Normalised tool kind (implementation-plan §3.10): Read/Glob/Grep and read_file map to read, Edit/Write and write_file/replace to write, Bash and run_shell_command to bash, WebFetch/WebSearch to web.

agent_type.description: The sub-agent that made the call (`apprentice`), from the hook payload; absent when the character itself did (implementation-plan §3.12).

stopped.description: The CLI stopped the sub-agent at its maxTurns (breakers.subagent_max_turns); absent when it finished on its own or the CLI did not say (implementation-plan §3.12).

data.description: The checks of the run the envelope's `attempt` names started, outside the Steward's tick (implementation-plan §3.1 "(P1-25)").

outcome.description: pass: every check passed, or none applied; fail: at least one failed; error: they could not run, a later tick runs them again; stopped: killed because the Steward stopped or the quest moved on.

checks.description: The checks that ran, in order (verdict.checks without their logs); empty unless pass or fail.

environment.description: fail only: the Steward set the run's checks aside because their environment failed (P1-54: Docker down, a container gone), so no judge reads them and they run again later. Without it a restarted Steward, the world and the metrics ledger could not tell such a run from a failing one.

check.description: The first failing check whose log showed its environment failed.

line.description: The line of its log that one of the territory's environment_errors found, masked.

data.description: In-band 'out of mana' signal, e.g. error rate_limit from source stop_failure or api_retry.

pool.description: PoolId from poolOf(tribe, model): the tribe id for a single-pool account (claude), or the adapter's pool (antigravity: gemini_models, claude_gpt_models).

model.description: The one model whose own cap this reads (argon, fable); absent for the whole pool. The pool's HUD band does not follow it (P1-32).

data.description: A gauge reached warn_margin_pct points below the cap: said once until its window resets or its figure falls back (implementation-plan §3.5, P1-22).

pool.description: PoolId from poolOf(tribe, model): the tribe id for a single-pool account (claude), or the adapter's pool (antigravity: gemini_models, claude_gpt_models).

model.description: The one model whose own cap warns (argon, fable); absent for the whole pool (P1-22).

data.description: The gauge that fell asleep: the whole pool, or the cap of one model (ADR 0009).

model.description: The one model whose own cap fell asleep or woke (argon, fable): only the characters on that model; absent for the whole pool (implementation-plan §3.5, P1-22). The pool's HUD band does not follow it.

resets_at.description: When the spent window resets, as the usage limit or the reading that put the gauge to sleep named it; the Steward probes just after (implementation-plan §3.5, P1-32).

data.description: The gauge that fell asleep (mana.exhausted) or woke (mana.restored): the whole pool, every character of it, or the cap of one model (ADR 0009).

model.description: The one model whose own cap fell asleep or woke (argon, fable): only the characters on that model; absent for the whole pool (implementation-plan §3.5, P1-22). The pool's HUD band does not follow it.

reputation.description: reputationOf(reputation.window): the avatar ring (--rep); pct null before any verdict.

title.description: titleOf(character): the tag shown over the head, if any.

kind.description: The command's `kind` (InboxCommand.kind), so the metrics ledger counts the owner's steps from the log alone; inbox/done/ names it for lines written before PS-01b.

data.description: The Steward applied the assignee's patch to paths of laws.patch_paths, which its CLI refuses to write, before the submit commit (implementation-plan §3.3, P1-28).

file.description: The patch file at the root of the plot, deleted once applied.

paths.description: What the patch changed, relative to the plot, '/' separators.

data.description: The Steward merged a party's part branches into its merge quest's branch, or tried to (implementation-plan §3.13, P1-21 (d)): before the machine's run and each knight's session, never before a judge's. A merge with nothing left to take in writes no line.

merged.description: The part branches this merge took in, in order.

pending.description: The part branches still not in, the one the merge stopped at first; empty once all are in.

stop.description: Why the merge stopped at the first pending branch: a conflict left in progress for the knight, a refusal by git or a hook, or a branch that is gone.

conflicts.description: With stop = conflict: the conflicted files, relative to the plot.

data.description: After a judge's session outside a scratch plot, the Steward put the quest's plot back to its commit: what the judge's commands left changed there (a generator, a formatter) is dropped, so the next session and the merge never take it for work (implementation-plan §3.15, P1-44).

paths.description: What was changed or new in the plot and is gone now, relative to the plot, '/' separators; an untracked folder is one path ending in '/'.

data.description: The Steward filed memos/<memo>.json from the Memos section of the quest's handover letter, as the run ended through a submit, a question or a crash. The line's actor is the character who wrote it.
The memo went where its kind's entry in registry/memos.json sends it (routeMemo).
The owner's decide_memo closed the memo; no quest changed.

quest.description: With decision = handled: the quest that does the work.

data.description: `elvaria upgrade` began building and trying a commit (implementation-plan §3.16.4).

ref.description: What the owner asked for (`--ref`), as typed.

to.description: A full commit id of the Elvaria repo: the name of the build folder `.builds/<sha>/`.

from.description: The pinned build; null when the kingdom had none.

data.description: Every trial passed: the pointer now names the new build; `from` is kept as the way back.

from.description: A full commit id of the Elvaria repo: the name of the build folder `.builds/<sha>/`.

to.description: A full commit id of the Elvaria repo: the name of the build folder `.builds/<sha>/`.

data.description: `elvaria upgrade --rollback`: the pointer went back from `from` to the build before it.
